subject: Architecture
title: The Roman Ponte Fabricio: Oldest Working Bridge
description: One-minute skill: The Roman Ponte Fabricio: Oldest Working Bridge.

hook.text: Rome's Ponte Fabricio was built in 62 BC and still carries pedestrians across the Tiber River today.

buildup.text: Its two stone arches span 187 feet, built from travertine and volcanic tufa by Lucius Fabricius.

discovery.text: An inscription on the bridge names the builder — rare proof of who designed an ancient Roman structure.

twist.text: The bridge survived floods, wars, and two millennia of use. Modern bridges often fail within 75 years.

climax.text: Roman bridge engineering spread across the empire — over 900 stone bridges were built in Europe alone.

punchline.text: A 2,000-year-old bridge. Still open. No maintenance budget needed.

quiz.question: When was the Ponte Fabricio built?
